prompt.context: Rock Energy, an Oil & Gas company, is evaluating buying one of three oil fields in South America. They plan to outsource all drilling activities after purchasing the rights to extract oil from one of the fields.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: What rights does Rock Energy get?
clarifying_info.a: The rights give Rock Energy the right to drill for 1 year and produce oil for 20 years. No oil production until beginning of year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many rigs can be deployed?
clarifying_info.a: A maximum of 10 rigs can be deployed in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost per rig per day include?
clarifying_info.a: Cost per rig per day includes crew, consumables, services, etc.
Any extracted oil will be sold at spot market price.
Assume oil wells will produce the same amount of oil for the next 20 years with no ongoing maintenance costs.

exhibits.title: Oil field profiles (2018)
exhibits.shows: A table and two bar charts showing drilling rates and average well depths by region, plus a summary table of operating parameters for Regions 1, 2, and 3.

data.note: Wells are continuously dug for one year only, with oil extracted going forward. Once a well is completed, a rig can move on to dig another well.

framework: Revenues: oil spot market price, daily oil field production per region, nature of extraction rights
Costs: drilling costs (rig costs, cost per rig per day), extraction rights costs (investment)
Profitability: number of wells drileable per year per region, total revenue, total cost, profit per region
Qualitative considerations: insurance costs, political stability, labor contracts/unions, oil price volatility, oil quality differences, other macroeconomic factors

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, how long does it take to drill one well in each region?
questions.guidance: Candidate should divide average well depth by drilling rate (penetration rate) to get days per well. Region 1: ~3600m / ~600m/day = 60 days; Region 2: ~3600m / ~400m/day = 90 days; Region 3: ~3600m / ~200m/day = 180 days.

math.setup: Time to complete well = Avg well depth (meters) / Drilling rate (meters per day)
steps: Note: casebook states answers of 60, 90, 180 days for Regions 1, 2, 3 respectively
math.answer: Region 1: 60 days, Region 2: 90 days, Region 3: 180 days

questions.prompt: How many wells can be drilled per year in each region (using 10 rigs and 360 days/year)?
questions.guidance: Number of wells per rig = 360 / days per well. Multiply by 10 rigs. Region 1: 6 wells/rig * 10 = 60; Region 2: 4 wells/rig * 10 = 40; Region 3: 2 wells/rig * 10 = 20.

math.setup: # Wells per year = (360 days / days per well) * # rigs
math.answer: Region 1: 60 wells, Region 2: 40 wells, Region 3: 20 wells

questions.prompt: What are the profits during year one of production (year 2 overall) in each region? Spot price is $50/barrel. Investment cost for extraction rights is $40M for each region.
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate: (1) cost per well = days per well * cost per rig per day; (2) annual revenue per well = price * barrels per day * 360; (3) profit per well = revenue - cost; (4) total revenue = revenue per well * wells per year; (5) total cost = cost per well * wells per year + $40M investment; (6) profit = total revenue - total cost. Key insight: Region 2 is most profitable overall despite lower margin per well than Region 1, because of the fixed $40M extraction rights cost and total volume.

math.setup: Cost per well = days_per_well * cost_per_rig_per_day; Annual revenue per well = $50 * barrels_per_day * 360; Total Cost = (cost_per_well * wells_per_year) + $40M investment; Profit = Total Revenue - Total Cost
steps: Region 1 total revenue = $1.8M * 60 = $108M; total cost = $0.3M*60 + $40M = $18M+$40M = $58M; profit = $50M
Region 2 total revenue = $3.6M * 40 = $144M; total cost = $0.9M*40 + $40M = $36M+$40M = $76M; profit = $68M
Region 3 total revenue = $5.4M * 20 = $108M; total cost = $3.6M*20 + $40M = $72M+$40M = $112M; profit = -$4M
math.answer: Region 1: $50M profit; Region 2: $68M profit; Region 3: -$4M loss

brainstorming.prompt: What qualitative issues would you consider when making an investment like this?

categories.name: Risk & Insurance
ideas: Insurance costs may differ across countries due to different regulations and coverage requirements
Political instability in South America could create additional operational or expropriation risks

categories.name: Market Factors
ideas: Oil price volatility — all regions have a negative return below approximately $27/barrel
Quality of oil extracted — lower quality oil could result in a sales price below spot market
Demand outlook and long-term price trajectory

categories.name: Operational Factors
ideas: Labor unions and contracts could affect drilling costs or timelines
Availability of skilled labor in each region
Infrastructure and logistics for transporting extracted oil

categories.name: Strategic Considerations
ideas: Option value of the 20-year production rights beyond year 1
Expected value analysis with different probability scenarios for barrels extracted per day

recommendation: Rock Energy should invest in buying the rights for Region 2, which generates the highest first-year profit of $68M

Although Region 1 has the highest profit margin per well (500% vs. 300%), Region 2 drills fewer wells at a higher production rate per well, and the fixed $40M extraction cost is spread over greater total revenue
Region 3 should be rejected as it generates a loss of $4M in year 1 and has the lowest margin per well
risks: Oil price volatility: all regions show negative returns below approximately $27/barrel, so a sustained price drop would eliminate Region 2's advantage
Political instability in South America could disrupt operations or threaten asset security
Labor or regulatory changes could alter drilling costs and affect profitability projections
next_steps: Conduct an expected value analysis assigning probabilities to different scenarios for barrels extracted per day
Assess insurance requirements and costs specific to Region 2's country
Evaluate political risk and stability indicators for the Region 2 country
Model long-term 20-year production cash flows to assess full investment return
